transcript.content: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I'm here because, well, lately I've been having this issue where I end up eating way more than I ever planned to. 

I'll get off a long shift working at the shop, and I'll just eat a ton of food all in one sitting. Like, I'll get a full fast-food meal, a bunch of snacks, and basically whatever else I can find in the fridge. It just kind of happens all at once, and I wanted to talk to someone about it.
During these episodes, do you feel unable to stop eating or control what or how much you eat?

Yeah, that's exactly what happens. Once I start on those nights, it feels like I just can't stop. It's like my hands just keep grabbing food, even while I’m sitting there telling myself to quit. I'll already be feeling sick to my stomach from how much I've had, but I just keep going anyway.
How often do these episodes of eating unusually large amounts occur?

Most weeks I have at least one night where I eat like that. It’s been going on for several months now. 

And... well, after I do it, I always try to make up for it. Like, I'll make myself throw up, or I'll take some laxatives. Sometimes I'll just skip my meals the next day, or work out extra hard to try and burn it all off. But yeah, it happens at least once a week.
How much does your weight or body shape affect how you judge yourself as a person?

It affects me a lot, honestly. I mean, I’ll look in the mirror before heading to the shop in the morning, and... well, if my stomach or chest looks soft to me, it just kind of ruins my whole mindset. It makes me feel like I’m sloppy at everything, you know? Not just how I look, but like I'm failing across the board. So yeah, my weight and shape definitely play a huge part in how I judge myself.
